A named piece in the documents (e.g. a dresser) must be placed at or near its text location; if the nearest valid place is more than 1 m away, the room layout must be adjusted to accommodate it.

A room whose name or drawn program is a dressing room (soyunma odası) is typed bedroom (or storage if it holds only a wardrobe and no bed), never 'other', so its program (wardrobe + mirror + seating) is checked and completed.

The ground floor's level mark (e.g. '+0,50' printed in the section) is the finished-floor datum of the building; the reading must set the ground floor to 0.00 m and read every other relative mark against it, not offset the whole building by the printed mark.

When a room's program group (e.g. dressing) has no place that passes the checks because the room is too small or the group is too large, the solver must either place a reduced version of the group or record the room as intentionally minimal, rather than silently adding nothing.
A small drawn piece around a level-mark text (e.g. '+0,50') is a level-mark symbol, not furniture, and must be recorded as such, not built as a piece.

A wardrobe (or tall storage) that blocks a door or window swing must be moved to a wall span that does not intersect the swing, or the door/window must be repositioned; the solver must not leave a tall piece blocking a swing when no free span exists, but instead flag the room layout as infeasible.

A kitchen must have its main functional anchors (fridge, hob/stove, sink, counter) placed as a coherent run; if the room's geometry does not allow the full run, the solver must place a reduced run and flag the missing anchors, not leave the kitchen without a hob or fridge.

A floor lamp whose model has a shade that is too large and sits at head height (blocking sightlines) must be swapped for a model with a proportionate shade and a height that does not block the room's main sightline.

A washbasin (or any fixture) that blocks a door or window swing must be moved to a position that does not intersect the swing, or the door/window must be repositioned; the solver must not leave a fixture blocking a swing when no valid spot exists, but instead flag the room layout as infeasible.

A large living room (e.g. 55 m2) must have its main furniture (sofa, coffee table, armchair) placed so that the main view shows them; if the room's geometry does not allow the full set, the solver must place a reduced set and flag the missing pieces, not leave the room bare.

A shoe cabinet (or any tall storage) under a sloped ceiling must be swapped for a model that fits the available height (at most the ceiling height at that point); the solver must not leave a crude, low-poly model when a real product of the type fits within the height constraint.
A drawn label for a piece (e.g., dresser) must be matched to a built piece within 1.0 m; if no place passes checks, the label is a false positive or the room layout is too constrained.
Furniture pieces must not overlap; if a clash is detected, the piece should be moved to the nearest free place.
Furniture must not cover openings (windows, doors); if a piece covers an opening, it should be moved to clear the opening.
When a section shows the ground floor at a non-zero elevation (e.g., +0.50), the reading stage must offset all plan-level marks by that amount to align with the section's datum.

rules_proposed.rule: When a tall wardrobe drawn against a wall blocks a door or window and cannot be moved (drawn lock, no free wall span), the solver must either shorten the wardrobe to a model that clears the opening or shift the opening, rather than leaving the blockage.

A kitchen must always contain a hob/stove and a fridge as part of its kitchen run; if the reading placed them but the group check reports them missing, the solver must re-anchor the kitchen run so the stove and fridge are present and counted, not drop them.
A floor lamp whose model has an oversized shade at head height is swapped for a library model of the same footprint with a correct proportion, not a generated model.

When a washbasin in a small bathroom blocks a door or window and cannot be moved (fixture move limit, clearance), the solver must reposition the door/window or choose a smaller basin that clears the opening, rather than leaving the blockage.

A large living room (salon) must always show its sofa and dining set in at least one interior view; if the camera cannot show them because of walkway constraints, the solver must adjust the furniture layout to free a camera point, not leave the room looking empty.

A shoe cabinet under a sloped ceiling must use a model whose height fits under the slope (at most the clearance height); if no library model fits, the solver must resize the cabinet or choose a lower model, not leave a crude placeholder.
A dining group must fit within the room's free spans; if no place passes checks, the group is not placed and the issue is flagged.
An entrance group must fit within the room's free spans; if no place passes checks, the group is not placed and the issue is flagged.
